entries.test: Publicly documented cases of workers being replaced by AI would test the claimed absence of proof.
entries.note: The surrounding text explicitly acknowledges some AI job losses and narrows the denial to replacement at scale and particular occupations.
The claim attributes private motives to the dealmakers; the deals and share sales alone cannot establish those motives.
The source concerns 'these' data centers, not AI data centers generally. The alternative that demand does not necessarily translate into spending asserts only a possibility.

entries.test: Aggregate generative AI revenue excluding OpenAI and Anthropic, compared with the costs of supporting one commercial AI data center, would test the claimed shortfall.
entries.note: Despite its dismissive phrasing, this makes an economic comparison with a factual core.

entries.test: An industry-wide financial collapse involving widespread failures of generative AI businesses would test the predicted collapse.
entries.note: In context, 'fiery apocalypse' expresses a firm prediction of industry collapse. No definite deadline is supplied.
The escalating descriptions of obscenity and ridiculousness supply no testable threshold.

entries.test: The three neoclouds' revenue disclosures and customer breakdowns would show their combined revenue excluding the five named customers.
entries.note: The surrounding analysis places the revenue estimate in 2025.

entries.test: AI compute providers' financial results and NVIDIA-backed neocloud contracts, debt financing and GPU purchases would test the claimed financing mechanism.
entries.note: The central mechanism has observable financial consequences. Its prediction of continued NVIDIA support has no deadline.

entries.test: Public customer contracts, compute usage and customer financial resources would show whether major customers other than OpenAI both need and can afford AI compute.
entries.note: The preceding questions supply the customer-market context included in the proposition.
The identity claim and insult are rhetorical. The adjacent 50% revenue estimate is a separate factual assertion.

entries.test: OpenAI's Oracle payment obligations, operating cash flows and available funds through September 2029 would establish whether it requires more than $290 billion in additional financing.
entries.note: Calling the number an estimate does not turn this firm funding requirement into a probability claim.
This evaluates the industry's health without committing to a specific financial condition or outcome.

entries.test: Anthropic's and OpenAI's revenue and cash-burn figures for 2025 through publication, alongside their full-year projections, would settle the numerical claims.
entries.note: The numerical assertions remain checkable despite the subjective description 'lethargic.'
He explicitly presents the architectural explanation as a theory and calls it likely.

entries.test: Reproducible evaluations of LLMs maintaining functional software, adapting to codebases and handling increasing code complexity would test the claimed limitations.
entries.note: The author adopts this explanation in his own voice, including the expressly identified paraphrase.

entries.test: Documented deployments in which AI performs software engineers' responsibilities and replaces their positions would test both the absence-of-proof and incapability claims.
entries.note: The claim concerns actual replacement of engineering work, beyond generating isolated code snippets.

entries.test: Controlled studies comparing engineers' completion times on comparable tasks with and without coding LLMs would test the claimed slowdown.
entries.note: The author states this generally, without restricting it to a particular study or task.

entries.test: Public AI sales, paid usage and customer commitments compared with infrastructure investment would test the asserted absence and inadequacy of demand.
entries.note: The assertion is broad, but demand has an ordinary commercial meaning in this context.
He explicitly labels the increase above $500 billion a guess.
The proposition changes media fear of criticizing powerful people into fear of telling the truth. It also replaces analysts' apparent unwillingness with asserted fear.

entries.test: Longitudinal GPU failure records, successor-product performance and resale-price histories would test the predicted failure, obsolescence and depreciation.
entries.note: Five years is an illustrative period, not a firm deadline.

entries.test: OpenAI's reported cash burn for 2025 and cumulative cash burn through 2030 would test the two stated amounts.
entries.note: The 2025 component is already due; the combined claim extends to 2030. 'If my estimates are right' qualifies the calculation rather than supplying an external triggering event.
The proposition attributes a private purpose and knowledge to NVIDIA.
OpenAI's eventual failure is independently testable. The full claim compares damage across alternative survival durations that cannot all be observed.

entries.test: If OpenAI fails, public measures of output losses, unemployment and financial-system distress would allow comparison with the pandemic and global financial crisis.
entries.note: The preceding paragraph supplies the explicit OpenAI-failure condition.

entries.test: Evidence linking continued AI promotion to retail investment exposure and subsequent AI-related losses in brokerage and retirement accounts would test the asserted harm.
entries.note: The financial-loss prediction is firm and has no deadline; establishing the media's causal contribution requires more than observing losses.

entries.test: Public evidence about the named coverage, resulting investment decisions and losses following an AI-market collapse would test whether such stories uniformly contribute to public harm.
entries.note: The universal 'every single' wording is a strong commitment. The predicted harm depends on the bubble bursting.
